_comment: Functions that ARE compiler output and should match, but have not yet.
They are held out of the work queue so waves stop rediscovering them,
and they are deliberately NOT counted as progress anywhere: a parked
function is still assembly, the ROM is still built from its asm/ unit,
and the C in work/<fn>/ does not go into src/decomp/.
This is a different claim from data/asm-resident.json. That file says
'no C will ever match this, because a compiler did not write it'.
This file says 'C should match this and ours does not yet'. Do not put
an entry here in asm-resident.json to get it out of the queue -- that
file is the evidence base for what hand-written assembly looks like,
and a wrong entry poisons every later judgement made from it.
An entry needs three things: the best percentage reached, the EXACT
remaining difference, and the axes already ruled out. Without the
ruled-out list the next wave repeats the same attempts -- which is the
specific failure this file exists to prevent.
TWO SHAPES ARE ACCEPTED and both are read as opaque by index_functions.
Older entries are a single prose string. PREFER THE OBJECT FORM for new
entries -- sub_0804FA2C is the worked example -- because it makes the
ruled-out list a real list instead of a sentence buried in prose:
bytes, best, remaining_diff, why_it_is_close,
axes_ruled_out[], settled_by_this_attempt[], reason
`settled_by_this_attempt` is the one that pays: it names derivations the
attempt PROVED, so an unpark does not re-litigate them.
Before parking anything, check the toolchain axis. The ROM was built
with two compilers and more than one flag set, and three functions were
parked as source-exhausted across two waves and permuter runs when the
source was never the axis. See data/compiler-overrides.json and the
'Per-file compiler and flags' section of docs/agbcc-codegen.md.
Unparking is the goal. Re-run `python tools/trymatch.py <fn>` against a
parked entry whenever a new codegen rule lands; the draft is kept at
work/<fn>/<fn>.c and best.c holds the closest attempt.
THE .rodata WALL IS GONE (wave 18, W18-B). Twelve entries here used to say
're-test when the split can express a .rodata word'. It can now. agbcc parks
a -fforce-addr address constant in the compiling unit's own .rodata, and in
this repo those same bytes also arrive as incbin'd ROM data in data/rodata.s
or data/data.s -- so a byte-exact honest draft could not be promoted, because
its word had nowhere to live and the blob was still supplying it.
tools/split_rodata.py now splits those blobs per symbol into generated pieces
under build/rodata (reading data/, never modifying it, exactly as
split_asm.py treats asm/), and gen_lds.py interleaves a promoted unit's own
.rodata between the pieces at the address the original build used. Declare
the words a unit owns with a `rodata` list in data/promoted.json.
ALL TWELVE were unparked this way -- sub_080081E0, sub_080083E0,
sub_0800977C, sub_0804E8F0, sub_0804FE10 and the seven-member sub_0805CA60
group, 3,368 bytes -- every one from a draft that names the global DIRECTLY,
with both builds reproducing the SHA1. See docs/agbcc-codegen.md.
COROLLARY, and it matters for what you keep in work/: when the honest
spelling is byte-exact and only its relocation differs, THAT draft is the
deliverable and the c_local workaround is not. Keep the honest one as
work/<fn>/<fn>.c. Three functions were held parked for several waves by
grinding on the workaround's register allocation when the honest draft had
been byte-exact the whole time.
DO NOT relax trymatch's reloc_equivalent to bless a .rodata word without
checking the placement exists. trymatch judges one unit; the split build
links all of them. A promoted unit whose .rodata the linker script does not
place either loses the word or shifts every address after it, and because
promote.py acts on trymatch's verdict the failure lands in the build with
functions already moved. Placement first, verifier second.

functions.sub_0801A6C0: 98.4% -- 64 bytes, size-exact, ONE byte differs at +0x2a. The original stores `strh r2, [r1, #0]`; every candidate produces `strh r3, [r1, #0]`. Both registers hold 0 at that point (r2 was just zeroed and stored to [r1, #4], r3 likewise), so this is a pure register-allocation tie-break with no source-level lever on it -- the instruction selection, the order and every other byte are already correct. Ruled out: the source axis, exhaustively, across two waves plus decomp-permuter runs; and the toolchain axis -- old_agbcc and dropping -fforce-addr were both tried after the wave-10 two-compiler finding and neither moves this byte. Not every allocation near-miss is a flag problem. Worth re-testing whenever a register-allocation rule lands in docs/agbcc-codegen.md.
functions.sub_08022618: 392 of 400 bytes, 8 SHORT (wave 15, C). Straight-line, 2 `.LC` pool words (gUnknown_080909A8 -> &gUnknown_08499580, gUnknown_080909AC -> &gUnknown_085D5ABC), both spelled with A2's `pp = &<word>` and both relocation-correct; `pp` stays in sl as the ROM has it. Every statement, the || chain, the four 2x2 tile stores and the two Div clamps are identified. The remaining 8 bytes are zero-extensions agbcc elides and the ROM keeps: `id`'s store truncation (`ldrb; lsls #0x10; lsrs #0x10`) is folded away by combine's nonzero_bits. The SAME effect on `ax`/`by` was worth 16 bytes and IS fixed, by spelling them `int` with an explicit `(u16)` cast at each use instead of `u16` locals -- see docs/agbcc-codegen.md. `int id` with `(u16)`/`(s16)` casts fixes id's 4 bytes and re-breaks ax/by, so the two want different spellings of one idea. Ruled out: old_agbcc (identical size); ax/by as dead entry parameters (identical output); 300 s of decomp-permuter from this draft (best 31.0%, no size improvement). Draft in work/sub_08022618/sub_08022618.c.
functions.sub_08042998: 444 of 472 bytes, 28 SHORT (wave 15, C). Straight-line, 2 `.LC` pool words (gUnknown_08091364 -> &gUnknown_030040D8, gUnknown_08091368 -> &gUnknown_085D5ABC) needing THREE different read-site spellings in one function (`**pp`, `w = *pp` then `*w`, `(*pp2)[i]`). Semantics complete: the bitfield model is struct Unk08499594's, which was derived from this function in an earlier wave. 12 of the 28 bytes are one thing -- the ROM emits both arms of the unk04_7 clamp in full, with two `.word 0xFFFFF87F` pool words, because its `cap` arm RE-LOADS `ldrb r0, [r0, #0xb]` rather than reusing the compare's value; agbcc CSEs that reload whether the field is read inline or through a local, so the two arms converge on the same registers and cross-jumping merges them. 4 more: gUnknown_08091368's `pp2` is const-propagated (two uses is under the threshold) so the second high register is never pushed. Ruled out: old_agbcc (identical size). Draft in work/sub_08042998/sub_08042998.c.
functions.sub_08058A2C: 400 of 392 bytes, 8 LONG (wave 15, C). Straight-line, 1 `.LC` pool word (gUnknown_0816D948 -> &gUnknown_030013B0, in the previously undocumented 0x0816D938-0x0816D9BC pool block). Semantics and the whole tail are exact. The 8 bytes are three separate allocation facts: (a) +2, `pp` is const-propagated at its second use so the pool word is emitted twice and `mov sl, r1` never appears -- TWO USES OF A `pp = &<word>` LOCAL IS NOT ENOUGH to keep it live, which is a boundary on wave-13 A2's `c_local` that was not previously recorded (sub_08022618 keeps the same idiom on four uses); (b) +4, the 0x417A pool constant lands in r8 instead of r4 and pays a `mov` at each of its two uses, downstream of (a); (c) +2, the `n` local is allocated to r1 and copied into r0 for __divsi3. Ruled out: old_agbcc (identical size); 300 s of decomp-permuter (best 75.8%, still +8); five spellings of the pool-word access. Draft in work/sub_08058A2C/sub_08058A2C.c.
functions.sub_0808B91C:
99.4% -- 496 bytes, size-exact, THREE bytes differ and they are one register-allocation choice: `v` (the final float result) is allocated r1 and the ROM allocates it r4, so `adds r4, r0, #0` and its two `adds r0, r4, #0` readers come out on r1. Every other instruction, every pool word and every relocation match. gcc's REG_ALLOC_ORDER offers the call-clobbered registers first and `v` crosses no call, so r1 is taken before r4 is considered; making `v` cross a call (`v = -v;` instead of `return -v;`) reshapes the tail and drops the whole function to 75.2%.

This is the tree's FIRST soft-float function, a cosf: range-reduce by whole pi, cosine Taylor series in r*r to the r^16 term, negate on odd n. Everything it established is in the 'Soft float' chapter of docs/agbcc-codegen.md and matters more than the three bytes -- double word order in registers is HIGH FIRST (FPA layout, so `ldr r2,=0x400921FB; ldr r3,=0x54442D18` is pi and not 9e97), every __*df3 comes from an UNSUFFIXED decimal constant promoting a float operand rather than from double source, `t - C` emits __subdf3 so an alternating series needs explicit negative literals with `+`, and the coefficients are 13-significant-digit hand-typed decimals that 1.0/24.0 does not reach.

Ruled out. TOOLCHAIN: default, old_agbcc without -fprologue-bugfix, no -fforce-addr, and both together all produce the IDENTICAL 99.4% and the same three bytes (tested by monkeypatching agbenv._OVERRIDES, leaving data/compiler-overrides.json alone). SOURCE: two 300 s decomp-permuter runs plus hand sweeps over the return form (`v = -v`, `?:`, explicit else, `n % 2`, `0.0f - v`, `n & 1` hoisted to a local), local declaration order, binding the quotient to a `double`, wrapping the tail and the return in their own do/while, and reusing the parameter for the square as well as the reduced value (+12 bytes: one long live range where the ROM has two that share r4).

NOTE on the draft: work/sub_0808B91C/sub_0808B91C.c carries a `do { } while (0)` around the two range-reduction statements. It is a diagnostic, not a claim about the source. Without it the file scores 97.6% with twelve differing bytes -- `x` lands in r6 and the x/pi quotient takes r4:r5 where the ROM has x in r4 and the quotient in r5:r6. The wrapper flips that because gcc weights allocno priority by LOOP DEPTH, so a zero-trip loop promotes everything inside it above everything outside; the original was more likely written through a macro. A cleaner way to raise x's priority would close nine of the twelve bytes and is the thing to look for first on any re-attempt.

sub_0804FA2C.remaining_diff: &gUnknown_03004580 is materialised early and register-allocated, but into sl and ONE INSTRUCTION BEFORE `ldr r5, =gUnknown_085D6A48`, where the ROM has it in r8 one instruction AFTER -- so the last two literal-pool words are swapped and the tile multiply pays two extra copies (`adds r3,r1,#0; muls r3,r0; adds r0,r3,#0` against the ROM's bare `muls r0, r1`). The multiply is downstream of the allocation, not independent: both operand orders and a temporary for the table read give byte-identical output.
sub_0804FA2C.why_it_is_close: This is the same failure mode that sub_0804D290 and sub_0804DCA8 had, and both of those are now MATCHED. Of two address constants used the same number of times in the same statements, agbcc gives the callee-saved register to whichever pseudo is created first and emits that one's ldr at the head of the statement; the fix on the twins was a comma operator inside the other argument's index, moving the reference one slot later. Here the identical comma costs &gUnknown_0300453C its r6 and is a net loss, because FA2C carries one more simultaneously live value than the twins do. See 'Of two address constants, the pseudo created FIRST wins the register' in docs/agbcc-codegen.md.
axes_ruled_out: old_agbcc -- 624 bytes on the twins, worse here too
-fno-force-addr -- BIT-IDENTICAL output, so these `ldr rN, =sym` are ordinary address loads and not -fforce-addr artefacts
lc_screen reports 0 pool words, so this failure mode is invisible to it
do { } while (0) round the tileNum statement, the sub_08057D44 statement, the sub_08015928 statement, or the four entry writes -- +8 to +20
the comma anchor in either the tileNum or the sub_08057D44 statement -- same +4 size, worse bytes
anchoring through pos, row, an int, or a register-qualified local -- all bit-identical, so the anchor's variable is irrelevant and only its position matters
a u16 (*)[8] pointer local for the gUnknown_03004580 reads -- collapses the base-plus-constant form the ROM CSEs into an ldrh displacement
two decomp-permuter runs of 300 s+ (3000 and 12000 iterations) -- best edits were noise (`new_var = 5` used as an array index) and both scored worse than the hand fix
settled_by_this_attempt: gUnknown_085D6A48's rows are STRUCTS, not u16[12] -- the ROM keeps column 9 in the ldrh displacement, which an array row cannot emit (4 bytes)
(rN = pos[k])[i*5+j] and not pos[k][i*5+j] -- the ROM builds the row address first (12 bytes)
ONE binding local PER STATEMENT: a single `row` reused across four statements is one pseudo spanning all of them and takes a low callee-saved register the ROM spends on the constant 180 (4 bytes)
* 0x100 and not << 8 (4 bytes)
sub_0804FA2C.reason: Register allocation, not source semantics. The instruction stream, the type model and every read form are settled and recorded in the draft's header; what remains is one address constant landing one slot early in a function that is one live value tighter than its two matched twins. Worth a wave-18 look precisely because the twins closed on the same axis.

sub_0804E7A8.remaining_diff: Three byte positions, and one of them is not a difference: the pool word relocates against `gUnknown_085D6C88 + 0xc` where the ROM uses `gUnknown_085D6C94 + 0` -- the same address, which reloc_equivalent would bless once the instruction stream is clean. The real residual is that the ROM emits `lsls rN,#16` beside EACH of the two tail subtractions and defers BOTH `asrs` past the gUnknown_03001FBC load, splitting each s16 conversion around the first argument's setup.
sub_0804E7A8.why_it_is_close: Its sibling sub_0804FCA4 MATCHES from the same shape and the same four spelling decisions; the two were solved by diffing them against EACH OTHER rather than against the ROM, which is what found the sound table's declaration. Everything except the two shift placements is the ROM's.
axes_ruled_out: s16 / u16 / int / short locals for the two computed arguments, `(s16)` casts at the call, inline arguments, reversed assignment order, separate declarations, an `idx` local for the first argument, and do/while(0) round each assignment, both assignments and the call.
Eight declaration orders and int/u16 for c, e, t, w.
Reaching the sound table as the flat `s16 [][6][2]` view its own pool word suggests: 136 bytes worse (52.7%). The struct-member spelling is required.
do/while(0) round the p1/p2 pair and round the `entry->x +=` statement.
settled_by_this_attempt: The 0x085D6C88 sound table is a STRUCT array reached as `g[B].unk0c[j][i]`, NOT the flat 3-D view. That single declaration is worth 40 points here and the whole match on sub_0804FCA4.
`&gUnknown_02029A10[c].entries[e]` CSEd across four member accesses needs the explicit byte-offset sum; used once (sub_0804E8F0) it needs the plain subscript.

`row = gUnknown_02028E5C[c]` must be bound INSIDE the subscript that uses it: as its own statement the two pool words come out in the wrong order (5 bytes), inline it loses the `[rB,#2]` displacement (44 bytes).

sub_0807166C.remaining_diff: The eleven-instruction prologue only; all eighteen case bodies and the jump table are byte-identical. The ROM has a->r4, b->r6, op->r5 and keeps the ORIGINAL cursor live, reading the second and third bytes as `[cur,#1]` and `[cur+1,#1]` and loading a->unk18 BEFORE the offset byte (`off + base`); the draft has a->r5, b->r4, op->r6, advances the cursor in place and adds `base + off`.
sub_0807166C.why_it_is_close: It is one opcode of a bytecode interpreter: three bytes off b->unk40, then a switch of six read-modify-writes and twelve comparisons whose twenty-four written-out arms cross-jump into the ROM's two shared tails.
axes_ruled_out: Eight declaration orders; int/u8/u32 for `op` and `v`.

`*b->unk40++` three times, an explicit `cur` local with three separate `b->unk40 = cur + n;` stores, `*cur++` with the write-back after each, and binding the offset byte to its own `int d` (21 bytes worse -- the offset must stay inside the address expression).
Both operand orders of `off + a->unk18`.
settled_by_this_attempt: `v` is a 32-BIT local, not `u8`: `u8` costs 15 bytes and `int` 4, while `u32` makes all eighteen case bodies byte-identical.
gUnknown_03005744 is a two-argument function pointer (from `_call_via_r2`) taking this function's own two context pointers.

The opcode map: 0-2 store/add/subtract an immediate, 3-5 the same through `a->unk18[operand]`, 6-11 compare against the immediate and 12-17 against `a->unk18[operand]`, in the order ==, !=, >, >=, <=, <.

sub_08079EA4.best: size-exact (264 bytes), 99.2% identical, exactly 2 bytes differ
sub_08079EA4.remaining_diff: The two bytes are the immediate field of ONE `bl` at +0x16, and nothing else in the function differs -- every other instruction, register and constant matches, and the only other diff lines are branch/reloc ADDRESSES that differ because the candidate sits at offset 0 while the original sits at +0x766 inside its unit. The original's instruction is `bl 3ec <_08079B38>`, an intra-file branch to a LOCAL label with the offset already assembled in and NO relocation. Any C caller necessarily emits `bl 0` plus an `R_ARM_THM_CALL` against an external name, so the bytes cannot agree. This is NOT a codegen difference and there is no source spelling that fixes it.
sub_08079EA4.why_it_is_close: 0x08079B38 is a genuine function entry that tools/split_asm.py merged into sub_08079B04, which is two bytes of `b _08079B38` sitting in front of the PREVIOUS function's 13-word literal pool and has zero callers. docs/agbcc-codegen.md already classifies this exact site under 'bl to a mid-function local label is NOT a tell' (the split-artefact row, `_08079B38` x3). The consequence for CALLERS had not been noticed: because `asm/` names the entry only as the local label `_08079B38` and no global symbol exists at 0x08079B38 in either build, a promoted C caller has nothing to link against. sub_08079EA4 is the first caller of such an entry that anyone has tried to match -- the only other site is `_08036B48`, whose two callers are both inside AgbMain, which is still assembly.
axes_ruled_out: the source axis for everything except the call -- the draft is instruction-for-instruction the ROM, so there is nothing left to derive

naming the callee `_08079B38` in C -- this WOULD make trymatch report a match, because both relocations would then name the identical symbol. It is a FALSE match and must not be used: `_08079B38` is a local (non-global) label in asm/code-0806CFC8.s, so the promoted unit would fail to link. This is exactly the class of error the brief warns trymatch cannot see, and it is the tempting wrong fix here.

an lds symbol (`sub_08079B38 = 0x08079B38;` from gen_lds.py) -- would make the split build LINK correctly and produce identical ROM bytes, but trymatch still rejects it: reloc_equivalent resolves ABS32 through the symbol table and requires a non-ABS32 relocation to name the IDENTICAL symbol, so `_08079B38` vs `sub_08079B38` is a mismatch regardless of both resolving to one address.
a function-pointer cast to the literal address -- emits a pool word and `bl _call_via_rN`, not a `bl`, so it is a different instruction stream
settled_by_this_attempt: the whole function's source is settled; the draft in work/sub_08079EA4/ is the deliverable the moment the symbol exists

the affine denominator is `proc->unk34 == 0x200 ? 2 : 0x200 - proc->unk34` and NOT the `d != 0 ? d : 2` form the promoted c_08027B68.c uses. Both are the same predicate; they are different code. The ROM presets `movs r1, #2` and conditionally overwrites it with `subs r1, r4, r2`, so the arm that gcc computes UNCONDITIONALLY is the `2`, which means `2` must be the TRUE arm in the source. The `!= 0` spelling put `0x200 - x` first and cost +4 bytes across the four call sites (two extra `adds r0, r2, #0` shuffles), scoring 28.8%. This is the general rule: in `c ? A : B` compiled to one branch, A is the arm emitted unconditionally -- read the presetting `movs` to recover which arm the source wrote first.
sub_080795A8 and sub_08079B38 both take TWO arguments with the first unused in the body; the proc pointer left sitting in r0 costs no instruction and is not evidence of arity, the `movs r1, #0` is

gUnknown_08615E40 is a real 12-byte u8 ROM table read `base + index; ldrb`, NOT a .LC pool word -- tools/lc_screen.py misclassifies it (fanin 1, density 4). Dereferenced against baserom.gba: 02 03 04 05 x3, with address-shaped words starting at +0x0c.
proc offsets: +0x30 int, +0x34 int, +0x40 int, +0x4c u16, +0x52 u16
sub_08079EA4.reason: TOOLING, not decompilation, and the fix is one line in the right place: tools/split_asm.py should treat a label that is the target of a `bl` from outside its own unit as a function boundary (there are 4 such sites, all listed in docs/agbcc-codegen.md), or failing that gen_lds.py should emit an absolute symbol at 0x08079B38 AND trymatch's reloc_equivalent should resolve R_ARM_THM_CALL through the symbol table the way it already does for R_ARM_ABS32. Either change unparks this immediately with no change to the draft. Deliberately NOT put in asm-resident.json: this is ordinary compiler output and the C is already right.

sub_0804F18C.remaining_diff: Register allocation only; the instruction stream and all the address arithmetic match. The ROM parks the 0xb4 gUnknown_02029A10 group stride in r8 and pays `mov rN, r8` at each of its five `muls` uses, and gives `pos` (the sub_08057D44 result) the low callee-saved r7. The draft does the opposite: the stride takes r6 and is used directly, and `pos` is pushed out to `ip`. That is why the candidate is SHORTER than the original rather than longer -- the ROM's extra bytes are the copies its own allocation costs it. Secondary, and downstream of the same choice: the ROM shares ONE `lsls #16; asrs #16` of `v` between the two uses and the draft emits it only at the second, because with one reference combine substitutes it into the first `strh`.
sub_0804F18C.why_it_is_close: Everything except the allocation is settled and verified. The three `.LC` pool words are REPRODUCED by the honest spelling -- agbcc emits &gUnknown_03001FBC, &gUnknown_0300451C and &gUnknown_0300453C into this unit's .rodata in the ROM's own slot order for 0x081360A0/A4/A8, and the text pool relocates R_ARM_ABS32 .rodata at three offsets, which is the placeable shape the twelve wave-18 unparks used. This is the same residual, in the same direction, as its matched twins sub_0804D290 / sub_0804DCA8 had before the zero-trip loop and the comma anchor closed them, and the same as parked sub_0804FA2C.
axes_ruled_out: The wave-13 `c_local` spelling (`&gUnknown_081360Ax` bound to a local, read `**local`) -- +28 bytes at 26.8%, kept as work/sub_0804F18C/_clocal_nearmiss.c. Worse on every axis than the honest draft and no longer needed for the relocations.

c_local with the MIDDLE level bound explicitly (`ppA = &LC; a = *ppA;` then `*a`), which is wave-13 finding (1) and is what the ROM's text literally shows -- 548 bytes (-24) at 10.8%: each `pp` has only two uses, agbcc const-propagates it at the second, and the high-register copy never appears. Two uses of a `pp = &<pool word>` local is not enough to keep it live, as sub_08058A2C already records.

`do { } while (0)` round the sub_08057D44 statement -- the lever that closed sub_0804D290. 548 bytes (-24), 35.5%: it moves the wrong way here, because D290 needed it together with two camera-origin pointer locals this function does not have.
`s16 v` versus `int v` with `(s16)v` at each use -- byte-identical, so the shared sign extension is not reachable by either.

`u16 (*t)[5][2]` with `t[side][slot][0]` versus `struct UnkPosPair *` with the flat `(e1 = &pos[side * 5 + slot])->x`. The flat form is correct and is what the draft carries: it reproduces the ROM's `lsls #2; adds; adds; lsls #2` single scaling exactly, where the 2-D form scales the two indices separately. F658 is the opposite way round -- its ROM really is 2-D with a 40-byte row.
TOOLCHAIN, all measured on the honest draft: old_agbcc, -fforce-mem, -fno-gcse and -fno-force-addr all leave it unchanged and none of them alters whether the .rodata words are emitted.
settled_by_this_attempt: The honest spelling REACHES this function's three `.LC` words, which the header comment on gUnknown_081360A0 and the wave-13 scalar/array triage both said it could not. What decides it is the candidate's CFG: with the two-bit guard spelled `if (a.bit0 && !a.bit6)` the tests fold to `(x & 0x41) == 1`, a basic block disappears, and agbcc emits NO .rodata at all. See docs/agbcc-codegen.md.

The guard is `t = *(u8 *)&gUnknown_03004504; if (t & 1) { if (!(t & 0x40)) ... }` -- six spellings probed and only this one gives the ROM's two separate mask tests with no QImode truncation on the second. sub_0804BCB8's own body has the identical shape over the same two bits.
gUnknown_0300454C[0] takes OamData.priority read straight back out of the field it was just assigned (`lsls #0x1c; lsrs #0x1e` on the stored byte), not a second literal 2.
The four gUnknown_03001470 writes are unk28 = gUnknown_0300451C * 8, unk2c = 0, unk30 = gUnknown_0300453C, unk34 = gUnknown_0300451C -- the same run its sibling F658 has minus the unk2c store.

sub_0804F658.remaining_diff: The same allocation residual as sub_0804F18C and in the same direction: the ROM keeps the 0xb4 group stride and the sub_08057D44 result in registers whose uses cost it copies the draft does not pay, so the candidate comes out short. The prologue, the four proc-field writes, the OamData bitfield run, both sub_08057D44 arguments, the two-bit guard and the whole 2-D position lookup are byte-identical to the original.
sub_0804F658.why_it_is_close: It was produced from sub_0804F18C's finished draft by five substitutions and reproduced that function's residual CLASS on the first trymatch, which is the banked-discount behaviour sub_0804DCA8 showed against sub_0804D290. Its three `.LC` words are reproduced by the honest spelling in the ROM's slot order for 0x081360B8/BC/C0.
axes_ruled_out: `do { } while (0)` round the sub_08057D44 statement -- 600 bytes at 17.2%, a large regression, so the D290 lever does not transfer to this member either.
`s16 v` versus `int v` with `(s16)v` at the one use -- byte-identical.
Everything ruled out for sub_0804F18C applies here unchanged; the two share the shape and, so far, the residual.
settled_by_this_attempt: The wave-13 scalar/array triage does not hold as a decision rule.
